name: Datalayer Agent Codemode, eval sandbox (default variant)
source: https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode (installed from the clone); sandbox from PyPI code-sandboxes (repo https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes)
pinned: agent-codemode 566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea (version 1.1.1), code-sandboxes 1.12.4 (tag v1.12.4 = d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5; installed files identical), mcp 2.3.0
engine: CPython exec() in the host process. Code that contains 'await ' is wrapped in an async function and run with asyncio.run() on the worker thread that CodeModeExecutor hands it to (asyncio.to_thread).
how_run: ToolRegistry with one stdio MCP server (lookup_server.py), CodeModeExecutor(registry, CodeModeConfig(sandbox_variant='eval')).setup(), then executor.execute(code, timeout=30), the call that the project's MCP server handler and pydantic-ai toolset make.

defaults.time: None enforced. execute() takes a timeout and the MCP server passes 30 s, but EvalSandbox.run_code documents 'timeout: Timeout in seconds (not enforced in this simple implementation)' (eval.py:166). P6 ran 120 s until the harness stopped it.
defaults.memory: None. P7 reached 4.4 GB host RSS in 2.3 s and was killed by the harness.
defaults.output: stdout, stderr and the last expression's repr all come back, untruncated (P2: all 200,000 A's plus 'RETURNED').
defaults.tool_calls: CodeModeConfig.max_tool_calls defaults to None (types.py:233); when set, executor.call_tool raises 'Tool call limit exceeded' (executor.py:1094-1096). Not reachable here because tool calls hang (P1).

hardened_config: sandbox_client=CodeSandboxClient.create(variant='eval', config=SandboxConfig(timeout=30, network_policy='none', env_vars={}, memory_limit=256 MiB, cpu_limit=1.0)) passed to CodeModeExecutor, plus CodeModeConfig(max_tool_calls=50) and execute(timeout=30). SandboxConfig fields at code_sandboxes/models.py:576-618; network_policy is the only one EvalSandbox reads (eval.py:406-455).

source_notes.finding: Typed Python bindings are generated on disk from each MCP server's tool list: one async function per tool in generated/mcp/<server>/<tool>.py, all calling generated/client.py call_tool(), which awaits a host-registered __call_tool__. Code imports them: 'from generated.mcp.probe import lookup'.

On demand: list_tool_names (fast, deferred tools hidden), search_tools (keyword overlap count over name plus description, not BM25 or embeddings) and get_tool_details. Tools can be marked defer_loading.

For eval, executor.call_tool is injected into the exec namespace as __call_tool__ and calls the host ToolRegistry's MCP client directly. The MCP session is created on the main event loop during discover_all, but the user code runs in asyncio.run() on a worker thread, so the first tool call waits forever on a session bound to another loop. P1 and P9 hung with 0 host calls over both stdio and streamable HTTP; out/P1-stack.txt shows the worker thread parked in asyncio.run inside eval.py _run_coroutine_sync.

None. The module and class docstrings say 'This sandbox does NOT provide security isolation. Do not use for executing untrusted code.' The namespace gets the real __builtins__. The project still makes eval the default sandbox_variant, and the docs call the sandbox 'isolated' ('Code executes in an isolated sandbox for safety').

network_policy='none' monkeypatches socket.create_connection and socket.socket.connect for the duration of run_code. That stopped urllib (hardened P3) but not a connect on the C-level _socket.socket class, which reached example.com:443 in both configs (P3x). The patch is also process-wide, so it briefly blocks the host's own sockets while sandbox code runs.

CodeModeExecutor.setup() copies the whole host environment into SandboxConfig.env_vars (env_vars = dict(os.environ)) for every variant, and execute() can inject OAuth identity tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN and others) into os.environ inside the sandbox. For eval the code shares the host's os.environ anyway (P5 read s3cr3t in both configs).
ExecutionResult carries stdout and stderr lines plus result reprs; the MCP server handler returns stdout, stderr and error fields. No truncation in either path.
Persistent: one exec namespace per context for the executor's lifetime (P8 printed 7). Variables assigned in async code are copied back from locals() into the namespace.
Exceptions become CodeError(name, value, traceback.format_exc()), so the message and '<sandbox>' line numbers survive (P10).

MCPClient.call_tool catches every exception and returns {'error': str(e)} instead of raising, so a failed tool call looks like a normal return value to the code (seen as {'error': 'Connection closed'} in the jupyter variant, datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P9d.txt). BSD-3-Clause, pushed 2026-11-21.

surprises: The default variant cannot call a tool: the first await on a generated binding hangs forever (P1, P9), over stdio and over HTTP. The README's Quick Start shows exactly this pattern.
execute(timeout=30) is accepted but not enforced for eval, so a hung tool call or an infinite loop never returns (P1, P6).
The docs page says code 'executes in an isolated sandbox for safety' while the default variant's own docstring says it provides no isolation (P4, P5, P12 all reach the host).
network_policy='none' is a monkeypatch that a raw _socket connect bypasses (P3x).
Every variant receives a copy of the full host environment through SandboxConfig.env_vars.
